title: Apology, regret and reconciliation
subtitle: a heartfelt apology, a lame excuse, a cast-iron alibi
summary: Learn the adjectives that collocate with apologies, excuses and alibis, the legal vocabulary of guilt and forgiveness, and the words for the different kinds of peace agreement.

lesson.heading: Apologies and excuses: collocations
lesson.note: A pretext is a pretended reason for doing something rather than the real one.

lesson.heading: Using the collocations
lesson.text: Each adjective carries a judgement. A **heartfelt** apology is felt deeply; a **lame** excuse is weak and unconvincing; a **cast-iron** alibi cannot be broken; a **phoney** explanation is a false one.

examples.text: He offered his most **heartfelt apology** for having offended everyone.
It was a rather **lame excuse**, and nobody really believed it.
The police were convinced the suspect's explanation was **phoney**, but could not prove it.
She had a **cast-iron alibi**: she had spent the whole day teaching at the local primary school.
examples.note: cast-iron = a firm reason why she was innocent

examples.text: He got an interview with her on the rather **flimsy pretext** of being interested in her research.
examples.note: flimsy = weak and not very believable

lesson.heading: Regretfulness in legal contexts
lesson.text: A court report packs a lot of this vocabulary into a few lines. When Jack Mosley was pronounced guilty of fraud, he showed no **remorse** whatsoever and was sentenced to ten years in prison. His three companions were **acquitted** of the crime and walked out free. Mosley later **repented** in prison and his sentence was reduced by one year.

examples.text: He showed no **remorse** for what he had done.
examples.note: remorse = feeling of guilt or regret

examples.text: All three of them were **acquitted** of the crime.
examples.note: acquit = declare not guilty; the noun is acquittal
repent = say you are sorry and ask for forgiveness; the noun is repentance

lesson.heading: Forgiveness and being cleared
lesson.text: Several formal verbs and nouns describe the official undoing of a punishment or an accusation. Notice that a **pardon** is granted, a **reprieve** is received, and a person is **exonerated** from blame.

examples.text: The President issued a **posthumous pardon** to the man, who had been wrongly accused of treason.
examples.note: posthumous pardon = official forgiveness after someone's death

examples.text: The Committee of Inquiry **exonerated** the Minister from all responsibility for the disaster.
examples.note: exonerate = declare someone free of blame

examples.text: The condemned man received a last-minute **reprieve** the day before he was due to be executed.
examples.note: reprieve = official order stopping or delaying punishment

examples.text: It is hard for the victims of crime to **forgive and forget**.
examples.note: These two verbs always come in this order.

lesson.heading: Peace and reconciliation
rows: written agreement between two or more countries
The two nations signed a peace **treaty** in 2014.
agreement to stop war while peace discussions take place
The generals from the opposing armies signed an **armistice**.
agreement between two enemies to stop fighting for a period of time
The two fighting politicians called a **truce**, agreeing to put their differences behind them.
There are fears that the current period of **accord** between the two sides is at risk of collapsing.
agreement to stop fighting in order to allow discussions about peace
Both sides have agreed to a **ceasefire** while talks are underway.

lesson.text: Remember the fixed order in **forgive and forget** - saying *forget and forgive* sounds wrong to a native speaker.

exercises.prompt: She had a ___ excuse for not mowing the lawn: she was allergic to grass.
exercises.explanation: A perfect excuse is one nobody can argue with.

exercises.prompt: He went around to her flat on the ___ pretext of wanting to borrow a book.
exercises.explanation: A flimsy pretext is a weak, unbelievable pretended reason.

exercises.prompt: The police had to let her go free, since she had a ___ alibi.
exercises.explanation: A cast-iron alibi is one that cannot be broken.

exercises.prompt: I want to offer you all my most ___ apology for the trouble I've caused.
exercises.explanation: Apology collocates with sincere and heartfelt.

exercises.prompt: The police have struck George off their list of suspects as he has a ___ alibi.
exercises.explanation: Alibis are cast-iron, convincing, perfect or phoney - never sincere.

exercises.prompt: Lauren's excuse for not coming to my party was pretty ___ - you'd have thought she could have come up with something better.
exercises.explanation: A lame excuse is a weak one.

exercises.prompt: The police officer asked us for a ___ explanation of the events leading up to the incident.
exercises.explanation: Explanation collocates with convincing, detailed and phoney; the officer wants a detailed one.

exercises.prompt: Kate sends ___ apologies for not coming with me this evening - she's got a bad dose of flu.

exercises.statement: The President granted him a repentance just an hour before he was due to be executed.
exercises.explanation: The President granted him a reprieve just an hour before he was due to be executed.

exercises.statement: He was exonerated of murder in 2014, but two years later was convicted of armed robbery.
exercises.explanation: He was acquitted of murder in 2014, but two years later was convicted of armed robbery. You are exonerated from blame, but acquitted of a crime.

exercises.statement: She showed a complete lack of remorse for her evil deeds and just laughed when the judge sentenced her.
exercises.explanation: Correct - a lack of remorse (or repentance) means no feeling of guilt at all.

exercises.statement: He treated her badly and she says she simply cannot forget and forgive.
exercises.explanation: He treated her badly and she says she simply cannot forgive and forget. The order is fixed.

exercises.prompt: Match each agreement with its definition.

pairs.right: written agreement between two or more countries
agreement to stop a war while peace discussions take place
agreement between two enemies to stop fighting for a period
agreement to stop fighting so that talks can happen

exercises.prompt: Ten years after his death, Daniel Taylor was given a ___ pardon by the government when another man confessed to the crime.
exercises.explanation: A posthumous pardon is official forgiveness granted after the person has died.

exercises.prompt: Rewrite Matt's apology using *apologised*: 'I'm sorry I broke your vase, Gina,' Matt said.
exercises.answer: Matt apologised to Gina for breaking her vase.
exercises.explanation: You apologise to someone for doing something.

exercises.prompt: Does each word belong to the courtroom or to peacemaking between countries?
